name: Zanda
one_liner: Cloud-based practice management for allied health with scheduling, notes, billing, and telehealth starting at $19/month.
short_description: Zanda (formerly Power Diary) is a cloud-based practice management platform for allied health clinics with scheduling, clinical notes, billing, and telehealth.
long_description: Zanda, formerly known as Power Diary, is a cloud-based practice management platform designed for allied health clinics including physiotherapists, chiropractors, psychologists, counselors, and massage therapists. The platform was rebranded in November 2024 to reflect the addition of AI-driven features while remaining the same core practice management software. Zanda offers appointment scheduling, client records, clinical notes, invoicing, online bookings, and secure telehealth. Pricing starts at $19/month (USD) for the Starter plan (1 user, up to 1,000 appointments) with the Growth plan at $49/month offering unlimited appointments and users. Additional practitioners can be added at $9.50/month. The platform is ISO 27001 certified and complies with HIPAA and GDPR standards. Zanda is particularly popular in Australia, UK, and among small allied health practices globally.
best_for: Allied health practices (physio, psych, chiro, massage)
Solo practitioners and small clinics wanting affordable pricing
not_for: Large health systems needing enterprise features
US practices requiring advanced insurance billing

faqs.q: Is Zanda the same as Power Diary?
faqs.a: Yes, Zanda is the rebranded name for Power Diary as of November 2024. It's the same practice management software with added AI-driven features.
Zanda starts at $19/month (USD) for the Starter plan with 1 user and up to 1,000 appointments. The Growth plan is $49/month with unlimited appointments. Additional practitioners are $9.50/month each.
Yes, Zanda is ISO 27001 certified and complies with both HIPAA and GDPR standards for protecting patient information.

faqs.q: What types of practices use Zanda?
faqs.a: Zanda is used by allied health practices including psychologists, physiotherapists, chiropractors, massage therapists, and counselors. Most users are small businesses with fewer than 50 employees.

company_info.notes: Zanda (formerly Power Diary) is popular globally, especially in Australia and UK for allied health practice management.
